candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Convert mixed numbers (and whole numbers when needed) into equivalent improper fractions or fractions with a specified denominator to enable computation.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three codebooks describe rewriting mixed numbers a b/c as (a·c+b)/c and rewriting whole numbers as equivalent fractions with a chosen denominator; B’s broader phrasing still matches the same conversion operation.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Determine a common denominator (often via LCM) and rewrite each fraction as an equivalent fraction over that denominator by scaling numerator and denominator.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three explicitly include selecting/using an LCM or common denominator and creating equivalent fractions by scaling; exclusions consistently separate this from cases where denominators already match.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Compute the difference of two rational numbers once they are in compatible forms (typically same denominator or separated whole and fractional parts), including recognizing results like 0 or an integer.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: Each expert defines the core subtraction step after alignment of forms (common denominator and/or mixed-number decomposition) and distinguishes it from setup (conversion/common denominator) and from post-processing (simplification).

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Reduce the computed fraction to lowest terms and/or express the final value in an accepted form such as a mixed number, improper fraction, integer, or 0.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three include reduction to lowest terms and optional conversion between improper fractions and mixed numbers/integers as a final formatting step, explicitly excluding earlier setup and the subtraction operation itself.

alignment_summary: Across A, B, and C, the same four skill concepts appear with near-identical boundaries: (1) converting mixed/whole numbers to improper/fraction form, (2) finding a common denominator and rewriting equivalent fractions, (3) performing the subtraction once forms are compatible, and (4) simplifying/formatting the final result. Every expert skill_id maps cleanly into one of these four shared concepts (all at 3/3 consensus).
